## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Markdown-to-HTML renderer for a comment box, with sanitization tested against real XSS vectors. /workspace/mini-md: src/render.js implements a subset by hand, no markdown libraries: paragraphs, bold with double asterisks, italics with single, inline code with backticks, fenced code blocks, links, and unordered lists. All source text is escaped before markup insertion; link hrefs must pass an allowlist (http, https, mailto, relative) and javascript: or data: urls render as plain text; rel noopener noreferrer and target blank go on every link. Tests with vitest and node-html-parser: each construct's structure, a payload suite including [click](javascript:alert(1)), in text, and a fenced block containing script tags rendered as escaped text inside pre code, asserting the parsed tree never contains script, img, or any on-prefixed attribute. Iterate to a green npx vitest run.

Summary of what was built: ## Files - **`/workspace/mini-md/src/render.js`** — hand-rolled renderer, no markdown libraries: - **Constructs**: paragraphs, `**bold**`, `*italic*` (bold checked before italic), `` `inline code` ``, fenced code blocks, `[links](url)`, `- / * / +` unordered lists - **Escaping model**: all source text is HTML-escaped (`escapeHtml`) *before* any markup tags are inserted, so raw HTML like `` can only ever surface as entities - **URL allowlist**: `isSafeUrl`/`sanitizeUrl` permit `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, and scheme-less relative URLs; everything else (including `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`) degrades the link to plain text `"text (url)"`. Control characters (`\t`, `\n`, etc.) are stripped before the scheme check to kill `java\tscript:` bypasses — browsers ignore those chars when parsing URLs - Every emitted `` carries `rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"` - **`/workspace/mini-md/test/render.test.js`** — vitest + node-html-parser: - Per-construct structural tests for each feature - A 23-vector XSS payload suite including the required `[click](javascript:alert(1))` and ``; each render is parsed and asserted to contain no `script`/`img`/`svg`/`iframe`/etc. nodes and no attribute matching `on*`, plus no surviving `javascript:`/`data:` hrefs - Fenced-block test verifies `` renders as escaped text inside `pre > code` ## Iteration notes (3 red → green fixes) 1. `java\tscript:alert(1)` passed the naive regex — fixed by stripping control chars pre-check and emitting only sanitized URLs 2. `- **bold** item` was misparsed as a paragraph due to an over-aggressive bullet guard — fixed by requiring whitespace after the bullet instead 3. node-html-parser treats `
` content as raw text (the inner `code` tag never becomes a DOM node), so the fenced-block assertion now inspects `pre.innerHTML` directly
